In plain language:

We took the “BOOK BRAIN VISUAL READER” idea out of your head and mine, put it into Grok’s hands, and asked:

“If a big public model uses this protocol, does it actually think better, or is it just pretty words?”

We tested it on 4 real topics. Here’s what we learned.

1. BTC test: “Is the chart lying?”
What we did:
Grok looked at BTC price using:

LEFT brain: APIs/text (CoinMarketCap, etc.).
RIGHT brain: a TradingView chart.
What happened:
Numbers matched. Trend matched. No invented spikes, patterns, or drama.

What we learned:
The protocol doesn’t break anything when things are clean.
It makes the model check instead of guessing, and it stayed honest to the data.

2. US vs China minerals: “Is this really a fight, or just a supply-chain fix?”
LEFT brain (text/data):

US wants a minerals trade bloc to reduce dependence on China.
China has ~70%+ share in key minerals.
US plans a $12B stockpile.
Actual goal: diversify and secure supply, not necessarily “declare war.”
RIGHT brain (visuals/headlines):

Headlines: “US counters China.”
Charts: big scary bars showing China dominance.
Photos: politicians at summits (showdown vibes).
What Grok saw:
Visuals made it feel like a geo-political fight, more than the data alone justified.

Lesson:
The protocol helped Grok say:

“Data: resilience + diversification.”
“Headlines: pushing rivalry and drama.”
That’s a big win: it separated reality from spin.

3. EU deepfakes: “Real problem vs horror-movie vibes”
